## Benchmark model–harness pairs, not models alone

Arena's HarnessTax study reports that, across seven models on two coding benchmarks, changing the harness moved API-equivalent cost much more than task success: Claude Code cost a geometric-mean 2.0× Pi on SWE-bench Lite, while average harness effects on success stayed within ±2 points. The 30-task-per-benchmark sample and unreleased raw traces limit generalization, but the result supports paired private evaluation with pinned harness versions, explicit context overhead, and total workflow cost. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-harness-choice-cost-correctness.md)

## Browser-agent claims require dependency-closure evidence

The popular `dots` repository is a thin CLI facade over an exactly pinned `invisible-playwright-mcp` package: local tests prove delegation and interface shape, while the dependency contains browser acquisition and conditional real-browser smoke tests. Those tests cover launch and basic page operations, not whether sites cannot detect or block the browser. Record both facade and engine revisions, distinguish artifact readiness from task success, and require authorized target-site trials before accepting anti-detection claims. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-agent-browser-facade-dependency-evidence.md)

## Multi-surface continuity needs more than a shared transcript

OpenDots separates conversational Threads from durable job attempts and committed effects. Its selected code paths use exclusive leases to reject stale completions, re-check current permissions during work, and look up a page-save receipt by thread and tool-call ID before retrying an ambiguous approved write. The project is alpha and Scout did not run its tests or connected services, but the implementation supports a reusable rule: preserve conversation context, work ownership, authorization, and effect receipts as distinct continuity layers. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-opendots-effect-recovery-multi-surface-agents.md)

## Proactive compaction must include the next action

AutoCompact trains a coding agent to choose a task-stage boundary, retain an actionable working state, and continue from it rather than waiting for token overflow. Its authors report 9.2- and 5.0-point absolute gains over the same base model on two coding benchmarks, including a 256K setting where no trajectory forced compaction. The study uses one model/scaffold and judge-corrected training, so the reusable lesson is an evaluation contract: test the trigger, retained obligations, and post-compaction behavior together, not summary quality alone. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-autocompact-policy-context.md)

## Causal evaluation needs an explicit intervention and replay boundary

Causeval packages repeated-measure uncertainty, three-valued release gates, judge audits, and counterfactual RAG and agent evaluation on top of DeepEval. Its replay code distinguishes recorded, live, and simulated tool behavior and refuses novel side effects by default. The project is alpha, its live studies are small and author-run, and Scout did not execute it; the useful contract is to preserve intervention, uncertainty, fidelity, and provenance separately rather than treating a causal label as proof. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-causeval-causal-llm-evaluation.md)

## Secretless sandboxes still carry identity and broker authority

Cordium keeps upstream application credentials behind an identity-aware proxy, associates each workspace with a revocable Session, and includes source-level end-to-end scenarios for network-policy changes. Its supervisor still holds renewable workspace identity tokens, and the rootless or constrained inner workload runs inside a privileged root Kubernetes supervisor pod. Review credential custody, permission to use the broker, token lifecycle, and outer-runtime privilege as separate boundaries rather than promoting “secretless” into “credential-free” or “least privilege.” [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-cordium-secretless-workspace-authority.md)

## Agent transparency should expose effective state, not configured intent

Kamchatka separates what the next model request will actually contain, what an allow/ask/deny decision covers, and what its Linux kernel really enforces. Its Landlock sandbox and seccomp socket gate are paired with explicit full, partial, unavailable, and heuristic fallback states. Scout inspected the pinned implementation but could not run its Rust tests; the reusable rule is to derive context, authority, and confinement claims from their owning runtime objects rather than collapsing them into one reassuring “sandboxed” label. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-kamchatka-inspectable-agent-boundary.md)

## Learn a source without making generated memory authoritative

SourceLearn turns repeated work over one stable source into a revisable model of its entities, conditions, procedures, and relations. Its authors report first place in 13 of 15 benchmark/backend settings, but their own audits find partially supported and unsupported units after task-guided rewriting. The useful boundary is to let experience identify what to reconsider, reconstruct durable knowledge from the versioned source, and retain direct retrieval and support audits rather than promoting the learned model into authority. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-sourcelearn-source-specific-competence.md)


## AI-attack reports need session-to-effect provenance

Huntback's Operation Open Ledger report says an intrusion crew installed and used `opencode`, retained a 772 MB agent database, and carried one borrowed component whose README credits ChatGPT. Those traces support agent presence and likely use, but the public report does not expose the agent sessions needed to attribute specific reconnaissance, exploit, or exfiltration effects to AI. Preserve an evidence ladder from installation through session chronology to independently verified effects; the report's more concrete control lesson is to monitor cloud-identity authority and bulk API use, because valid OAuth credentials can exfiltrate an ERP without endpoint malware. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-open-ledger-ai-assistance-evidence-boundary.md)

## Agent UI contracts still need implementation conformance

Bricks models interface components as project-relative semantic contracts: agents inspect the target system first, define responsibility and reachable states, reuse product primitives, and verify on the real page. Its current `npm test` only checks catalog structure, reference existence, and basic skill frontmatter; it does not establish that generated UI follows those behavioral contracts. Keep semantic guidance, project binding, structural validation, and rendered task-path conformance as separate evidence layers. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-bricks-agent-ui-contracts-enforcement-gap.md)

## XHS interest in harness self-improvement kept growing

A current read of 机器之心's XHS summary of Lilian Weng's harness-engineering essay shows engagement rising from 58 likes in Scout's July snapshot to 643 likes and 899 saves. The post translates harness optimization into three practitioner patterns—closed-loop runtime, filesystem-backed memory, and child-agent/process management—and presents the harness itself as an optimization target. This is evidence about the XHS summary and audience response, not independent verification of every claim in the original essay. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-07-08-xhs-scan-73.md#1-weng-li-self-improvements-realistic-path-is-harness-optimization-high)

## Guardrails are model-policy-deployment pairs

A Red Hat benchmark found no universally superior guardrail paradigm: on prompt injection, a 200M task-trained classifier nearly matched a 35B LLM judge at much lower reported median latency, while content-safety rankings shifted across models and policy wording. One Laya-specific policy raised Laya from 57.87% to 75.20% but lowered Jev from 86.20% to 82.53%. Benchmark the exact model, policy, threshold, serving path, and traffic distribution; input filtering remains a fallible control rather than an agent authority boundary. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-decision-model-guardrail-benchmark.md)

## Persistent skill changes need candidate and integration gates

RPG revises a robot's shared skill code and prompt from simulation failures, evaluates each candidate across 22 tasks, and retests the merged system before retention. The authors report improvement from 28.6% to 95.0% across 15 rounds, but held-out performance still dips after two accepted rounds and towel folding remains unreliable. Use failure-triggered edits as proposals, preserve an accepted rollback state, and test both candidates and their integrated result; a fixed low-sample gate is not proof of non-regression. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-guided-self-improvement-embodied-agents.md)

## Production-trace task extraction is a versioned inference

Laminar reports reducing task-extraction LLM cost by clustering similar recent agent turns, hashing their shared line structure as a prompt-template version, and generating one regex per version. The design turns repeated traces into a cheap parser cache, but the extracted string is still a fallible, version-scoped label—not authenticated user intent or an evaluation oracle. Preserve the template hash, regex revision, extraction path, confidence, and original trace when production tasks feed analytics or evals. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-production-trace-task-extraction.md)

## Conversation continuity is not execution continuity

Jelly keeps raw history and activity separate from the model's last successful working-context checkpoint. Its crash test kills an active run, verifies that it returns as visibly interrupted, and continues only from prior successful context; incomplete tool work is neither admitted nor replayed. Scout did not run the test, and Jelly is a trusted-user local tool rather than a durable effect engine, but the implementation supports a safe baseline: preserve identity and audit history while leaving ambiguous work interrupted. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-jelly-successful-context-interruption-boundary.md)

## Production-agent evaluation is resonating as failure reconstruction

A current reread of a pseudonymous XHS account of six Agent-developer interviews shows engagement rising from 976 to 1,405 likes and from 1,196 to 1,695 saves. Its useful contribution is not the unverifiable hiring claim but a probe design: inject malformed tool results, timeouts, repeated calls, context loss, and partial branch failure, then test whether the operator or system can reconstruct detection, diagnosis, containment, and replay. The author also promotes paid training in replies, so popularity measures interest rather than validity. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/agent-evaluation.md#xhs-practitioner-signal-test-incident-reasoning-not-framework-recall)

## Crash resilience has three checkpoints

Agent SDK for Go journals completed LLM and tool steps, but its source makes the remaining cut points visible: an in-flight tool can repeat after its external effect, and a stream consumer can checkpoint an offset before it processes the corresponding event. Treat runtime history, business-effect settlement, and consumer progress as separate facts; use provider idempotency or reconciliation for tools and an idempotent or transactional inbox for stream handling. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-agent-sdk-go-durability-boundaries.md)

## Failure logs should record who—or what—actually detected the incident

Nothing Threw's expanded five-month catalogue reports 74 production-agent incidents: 9 were caught by a deterministic gate or surfaced error, while 45 appeared only in a later investigation. Its LLM reviewer caught three new incidents but was running under an improvised identity, showing why evaluations should retain detector type, effective runtime identity, execution coverage, and verdict policy rather than a single “automated” flag. The catalogue is one operator's selected retrospective, and both of its live-system audits found an error in the catalogue itself. [Updated note](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/agent-evaluation.md#record-how-failures-were-detected-not-only-what-failed--nothing-threw-hngithub-sepoct-2026)

## Completion checks need content and configuration identities

The independent `Shashankss1205/OpenDots` runtime accepts a required check only while both its workspace fingerprint and its command-plus-sandbox signature still match, and rechecks after retaining the final artifact. Its repository-authored tests cover edits during review, changed check commands, self-mutating checks, and unsigned legacy evidence; Scout did not run them. Bind local completion receipts to exact bytes, predicates, execution boundaries, and artifacts, while keeping external-effect settlement separate. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-opendots-content-bound-completion-evidence.md)

## Browser bridges inherit the authenticated session's authority

`figma-server` replaces Figma's approved-client MCP path with a loopback bridge to a dedicated signed-in Chromium profile. Its managed leases, file locks, URL checks, and private receipts reduce some hazards, but arbitrary JavaScript and raw CDP can bypass file coordination, reach shared browser state, and leave the worker in raw mode until browser restart. Evaluate account authority, transport admission, managed controls, escape surfaces, mode lifetime, and effect evidence separately; a dedicated profile is still a durable credential container. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-figma-browser-bridge-authority.md)

## Derived memory should expire with its evidence epoch

Sibyl binds promoted graph memory to source revisions and snapshot identity, makes an old derivative non-recallable after an evidence-bearing source change, and reports incomplete correction propagation rather than claiming every projection was updated. Its repository-authored tests also reject a correction-and-restore round trip as the original epoch even when the text matches again. Scout inspected but did not run those tests; the reusable rule is to revalidate derived memory at publication and retrieval, preserve old lineage, and track invalidation until every readable projection is reconciled. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-02-sibyl-source-versioned-memory-validity.md)

## Raw visual evidence can outlive the model context

VISTA archives every returned frame outside the model context and lets an agent retrieve arbitrary earlier frames, crops, and exact pixels when its question changes. Its author-run ARC-AGI-3 ablation jumps from 70.05 RHAE with compact notes to 94.10 after adding archived-frame inspection, but the public tasks may have appeared in post-benchmark model training and the default run averages 30.7 million tokens per game. Treat “lossless memory” as retained source bytes—not reliable recall—and keep raw evidence, derived notes, bounded context, and effectful actions separate. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-03-visual-harness-retrievable-frame-memory.md)

## Secret cleanup needs separate copy and containment evidence

Agent Scrub treats coding-agent transcripts, tool output, memory, file snapshots, and selected databases as additional secret copies. Its source defers active files, verifies exact preimages and parseability, and blocks “clean” claims when stores are unreadable or unsupported. That makes local redaction safer, but it does not rotate the credential, audit prior use, or remove provider-side and backup copies. Preserve copy inventory, scan coverage, mutation receipts, and credential containment as separate facts. [Finding](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-03-agent-history-secret-redaction-boundary.md)

## Tool selection is not argument correctness

[KaliBench](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-03-kalibench-command-structure-evaluation.md) separates choosing a CLI tool from constructing its flags and positional arguments. In the authors' evaluation, narrowing the candidate set mostly fixed tool selection, while supplying tool documentation drove much larger command-accuracy gains. Its runtime-free reward is useful for structural regression testing, but matching a prevalidated reference command does not prove a new command is safe, equivalent, authorized, or effective in a live environment.

## Documents are auditable memory, but still need evidence and routing

[Operator Memory](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/hn-agent-operational-memory.md#documents-are-an-auditable-memory-layer-not-a-complete-memory-replacement-oct-2026) makes a concrete case for maintained Markdown, explicit catalogs, and reviewable Git history instead of opaque top-k memory injection. The useful boundary is narrower than its headline: documents are strong candidates for admitted project truth, while raw archives remain necessary for audit and re-derivation, and indexes or retrieval remain fallible routes rather than proof that context is current or complete.

## Stale skills need counterfactual runs and immutable anchors

[SkillAudit](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-03-skillaudit-agent-skill-maintenance.md) is described in an XHS post as comparing the same task with and without its current skill, locating harmful guidance from trajectory differences, and rolling back edits that violate task-derived anchors. The control pattern is useful, but the reported 73.9% reward remains an unverified secondary-source claim because the post links no paper, code, task list, evaluator details, or run history.

## Context quarantine does not guarantee least authority

[Late CLI](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-03-late-cli-context-isolated-orchestration.md) gives delegated workers fresh histories and removes built-in file-writing tools from its lead agent, concretely separating planning context from execution noise. But workers first inherit almost every live parent tool—including MCP and plugin tools—so a role's declared tool list is not the final authority boundary. Effective post-composition capabilities need their own audit, separate from context isolation.

## Local signatures do not create principal separation

[Agent Blackbox](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-09-14-audit-integrity-needs-external-tail-anchor.md#follow-up-local-signing-is-not-an-independent-trust-boundary) pairs a hash-chained, signed local ledger with pre-tool security rules, while candidly documenting the trust boundary: under the default same-user deployment, an agent-controlled process can reach the evidence and signing keys. Independent anchors, recorder availability, fail mode, and OS-level principal separation remain distinct from a passing chain verification.

## Consequence grading catches structurally valid failures

[Argo-Bench](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-04-argo-bench-consequence-scored-data-agents.md) evaluates 210 data-agent workflows by the forecasts, reports, allocations, and enforcement actions agents file against hidden simulator state—not by query similarity. The authors report that 66.9% of dashboard data sources that passed their structural contract still scored zero on values, illustrating why executable SQL and valid schemas are only intermediate checks. Its simulated warehouse is deliberately cleaner than a mature enterprise system, so the reusable signal is the separation of navigation, analysis, commitment, and consequence rather than the leaderboard as a measure of real-company readiness.

## Draft autonomously; approve the exact external effect

[Elves](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/findings/2026-10-04-unattended-drafting-review-boundary.md) offers a concrete asymmetric-autonomy pattern: scheduled agents may scan configured sources and produce reviewable drafts, while connector write tools are denied and external release remains human-gated. That moves attention from approving agent startup to judging an actual artifact, but “nothing ships” is not “nothing consequential happens”: intake, triage, sensitive local retention, prompt injection, and effective tool-composition coverage still need separate controls and evidence.

## Authority migration needs equivalence and absence proof

[HOL Guard](/app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge/agent-security-enforcement-evidence.md#follow-up-moving-an-enforcement-oracle-needs-both-equivalence-and-absence-proof) treats moving hook decisions from a Python semantic evaluator into Rust as two proof obligations: map safety-relevant behavior to tests of the new production path, and prove the retired evaluator cannot execute through source, lazy imports, packaged copies, environment switches, or test-only routes. A passing replacement suite is only half the migration if old authority remains reachable; deletion is only half if adversarial behavior disappeared with it.
